title: Linearity and invertibility of the specified stalk class map
statement: Let f:X→Y be a scheme morphism, y∈Y, F an O_X-module, p≥0, A=O_{Y,y}, c:Spec A→Y, X′=Spec A×_Y X, f′ the first projection, g′ the second projection, and F′=g′*F. Let C=H^p(X′,F′) with A-scalars through Gamma-Spec followed by f′.appTop, and S=(c_*R^p f′_*F′)_y. For b of [def-weil-pbc-local-direct-image-stalk-class-map], there exists an A-linear equivalence e:C≃S satisfying e(x)=b(x) for every x∈C. This determines e uniquely. No compatibility with independently supplied restricted resolutions is asserted here.

source.place: Lemma 20.7.3 (Tag 01E4); Lemma 30.20.7 (Tag 02OD), displayed stalk/global-cohomology equality, expanded using exact closed-point evaluation. No formal-functions hypotheses are needed for this subargument.

proof.text: On a local spectrum every neighborhood of its closed point is top. Use Mathlib exists_germ_eq and germ_eq to prove the top germ of any abelian presheaf bijective. The sectionCohomologyComparison is an isomorphism: its homology comparison is an isomorphism, and the counit is a componentwise isomorphism of complexes. Underlying theta is the sheafification unit followed by this comparison. Its stalk is an isomorphism by stalkFunctor_map_unit_toSheafify_isIso. The germ naturality square and the two bijective top germs imply that theta on top is bijective.

For c = fromSpecStalk y, Mathlib preimage_eq_top_of_closedPoint_mem and fromSpecStalk_closedPoint show that every neighborhood of y has inverse image top. Consequently every restriction of c_*N between such neighborhoods is an isomorphism: it is the image of the unique isomorphism between the equal inverse-image opens. The germ representative and germ equality lemmas then prove the top germ into (c_*N)_y bijective. Expand the actual class map. resolutionSectionClass is an isomorphism on top by step 1 and its other specified resolution/evaluation homology isomorphisms. The next resolution comparison on sections is also an isomorphism. Compose these two bijections with the pushforward top germ bijection. This proves bijectivity of the specified additive map without any new hole.

Use the separate scalar compatibility theorem to equip the given additive map with a linear-map structure. Apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective to this very linear map using step 2. Its underlying function is definitionally the specified class map, so the required pointwise equality is reflexivity. No arbitrary witness or repackaged equivalence is used.

theorem localDirectImage_stalk_cohomology_equiv {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : Y)
    (F : X.Modules) (p : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology (pullback (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f).toRingedSpace p ⋙
        ModuleCat.restrictScalars
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of (Y.presheaf.stalk y))).inv ≫
            (pullback.fst (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f).appTop).hom).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.snd (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f)).obj F)
      ≃ₗ[Y.presheaf.stalk y]
      (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace y).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Y.fromSpecStalk y)).obj
        (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.fst (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f)).rightDerived
          p).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.snd (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f)).obj F))),
      ∀ x, e x = localDirectImage_stalk_class f y F p x
